subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Representativeness Heuristic
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Representativeness Heuristic.

hook.text: She's quiet and wears glasses. People guess librarian over salesperson despite 75x more salespeople.

buildup.text: We judge likelihood by how well someone fits a stereotype, not by actual statistical frequency.

discovery.text: Representativeness heuristic: if it looks like a duck, we call it a duck, ignoring the base rates.

twist.text: Coin flip HHHTTT feels 'less random' than HTTHHT, but both are equally probable sequences.

climax.text: Stereotypes feel accurate because they match patterns. But matching a pattern doesn't make it likely.

punchline.text: Looking the part doesn't mean playing it.

quiz.question: What does the representativeness heuristic cause us to do?
options: Judge by how well something fits a stereotype
